correctness.rationale: For dimension k>=1, reduced row-echelon pivots force k<=4; summing weights over all binary codewords of a full-support rank-k generator yields s2^(k-1)<=4(2^k-1), hence s<=7. The exact finite rank-by-column-multiplicity formula counts full-rank matrices with no zero column and every row combination of weight<=4, with free GL(k,2) quotient. Two exact, independently organized exhaustive enumerators in verify.py agreed in all forty cells. The exact-support bijection produces the all-length formula; the rank-four seven-support case is excluded by a second moment inequality, and Walsh inversion gives the unique rank-three seven-support simplex type and 30 labelled copies. No infinite conclusion is extrapolated from finite-length sampling.

originality.rationale: The closest published paper arXiv:2610.31618v1 states generic polynomiality and an unevaluated support-coefficient decomposition, not the fully evaluated binary diameter-four all-rank table. Theorem 2.20 of arXiv:2512.17542v1 covers structural classification only for dimension equal to maximum weight and does not imply the lower-rank exact counts. Literature and mathematical-record searches did not find an exact covering table, although an obscure historical equivalent cannot be excluded.
